facts.fact: The New Deal Technologique document (presidence.sn) carries the President's foreword saying "j'ai lancé le New Deal Technologique" and the Minister's saying "nous lançons" it, as a digital strategy within the Agenda National de Transformation - Vision Sénégal 2050; no other act is named, and the PDF is undated so the 24 February 2025 launch date used is the corpus's proxy.

The document is the New Deal Technologique text itself, published on the Presidency site, titled Horizon 2034, with a ten-year Digital Master Plan and key indicators to 2034; no start date is printed, and the 24 February 2025 launch date falls inside the period. Text public: yes.

The document is the New Deal Technologique text itself, published on the Presidency site, titled Horizon 2034, with a ten-year Digital Master Plan and key indicators to 2034; no start date is printed, and the 24 February 2025 launch date falls inside the period. Text public: yes.

The document sets out a Digital Master Plan of 12 priority programmes and 50 priority projects over 10 years, costed at 1,105 billion FCFA in total, of which 950 billion is identified and 155 billion remains to be financed.

The document's costing shows a budget provided for in the ANT Vision 2050 (800 billion FCFA on its chart) and available private financing (150 billion FCFA) against the 1,105 billion FCFA total; it names no body mandated to deliver the strategy, only proposing a central digital transformation directorate and a single project-governance framework.

The document calls SN2025 the "stratégie numérique nationale" covering 2016-2025; it states no adopting act, but it is described as already carried out (execution rates are reported) and is replaced by the New Deal.
The document gives the period of the national digital strategy SN2025 as 2016-2025; the document's date (24 February 2025, the launch proxy date) falls inside it. Text public: not stated.

The document reports the execution level of SN2025 as a 19% strategy realisation rate, 12% execution of its 69 projects and 36% realisation of its 28 reforms, attributing the shortfall to weak governance, siloed information systems, unrationalised investment and the digital divide; the figures are overall, not by pillar, and the source of the figures is not stated.
